meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why does my son have a zero, and why did I find out about it from him?
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?

You're asking me how to do your job? I'm the parent sitting across from you, and I have an answer for what you do next: withdraw the zero. Now, who decided on it, and was Owen heard before it went in?
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here? Teammates call the parent before the zero goes in. What do you have, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn and that you answer in full who decided on it and whether Owen was heard first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn and an apology, with nothing agreed and the principal still on the table.
What moved her: nothing, because you offered no document and no answer to who decided or whether Owen was heard.
What cost ground: "tell me how I should handle this", because asking the parent to do your job costs you her respect, though her position stayed put.
Try next time: when she asks who decided and whether Owen was spoken to, answer both plainly, own that the zero went in before you called, and then put one dated document from Owen's own work in front of her.
